# echook

> echook tells you what your coding agent is doing when you cannot see it: a sound, spoken summary, desktop toast or webhook on Claude Code, Cursor and Codex lifecycle events, plus a status line. An AI agent installs, configures and removes it through one non-interactive CLI, `audio-hooks` (JSON in, JSON out). Nothing is hand-edited.

- Live truth for every subcommand, hook, config key, error code and env var: run `audio-hooks manifest`.
- [Agent guide](AGENTS.md): the rules, a map of the repository, and which document to read before changing each area.
- [Install, upgrade, remove](docs/INSTALLATION_GUIDE.md): the commands per editor and the one step a person must type.
- [Mapping a plain-language request to commands](plugins/audio-hooks/skills/audio-hooks/SKILL.md).
- [Privacy](PRIVACY.md): what is stored locally, and the one case (a webhook the user configured) in which data leaves the machine.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md).

Scope: notification and the status line only. Timers, wellness prompts, gamification, opening URLs and side-commands are out of scope by design.
